tools.name: session_brief
tools.description: What changed for the stack you run since your last call: retired models, price changes, deprecated packages, pick changes. Use at session start if your code calls third-party APIs. Send provider, model and package ids (never a manifest) and your last cursor. Returns clear|changed|attention, at most

tools.name: rescue
tools.description: Diagnose a failing third-party API call before you retry or swap: paste the exact error (429, 402, 529 overloaded, insufficient_quota, model_not_found, deprecated SDK) and provider id. Returns the cause, an immediate fix and a fallback route, or no match plus checks to run. Not for picking a provide

tools.name: decide
tools.description: Choose a provider before writing integration code: LLM API, code sandbox, vector DB, web search, email, Postgres, auth, browser, observability. Send task in words or a jtbd id. Returns the dated editorial Depot Pick, a runner-up, the pick's price with source URL and date, and when not to take it. Fo

tools.name: depot
tools.description: Lookups beyond one pick; one op per call, args as an object: quote(jtbd) sourced SKU prices; estimate(jtbd, workload) monthly cost; compare(providers); free(jtbd) $0/OSS rows; check(providers) deprecated/retired flags; audit_repo(packages, models); stack(task), bundle(jtbds); search(q); kit(class);

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "session_brief" stacks urgency/override words (never, attention). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp?via=mcp-registry" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: session_brief, rescue.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: decide · Private data: decide · Public sink: session_brief, decide · Destructive: session_brief, rescue

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
